title: Addressing Gaps Identified in Financial Action Task Force's Recent Assessment of Singapore
what_it_is: Addressing Gaps Identified in Financial Action Task Force's Recent Assessment of Singapore

sections.label: FATF assessment of Singapore
sections.summary: Questions ask how the Government will address FATF findings on beneficial ownership verification, mutual legal assistance delays, cooperation channels and asset recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law in view of the Paris-based Financial Action Task Force’s assessment that Singapore is partially compliant in implementing technical requirements on transparency and beneficial ownership of legal persons and legal arrangements, how is the Government planning to address gaps in relation to verification requirements and the accuracy of beneficial ownership information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law in view of the findings of the Mutual Evaluation Report of Singapore published in May 2026 by the Paris-based Financial Action Task Force, what steps will be taken to (i) reduce delays in addressing mutual legal assistance requests (ii) increase the use of formal and informal cooperation channels in transnational crime investigations and (iii) accelerate asset recovery efforts from abroad.

sections.label: Singapore on FATF follow-up
sections.summary: The FATF placed Singapore on regular follow-up, the category for countries assessed to have performed well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In recognition of this, the FATF has placed Singapore on regular follow-up, which is the category for countries that have been assessed to have performed well.

sections.label: Timelines for mutual legal assistance
sections.summary: Straightforward requests are executed in as little as three days, while complex requests take about 10 weeks on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Straightforward requests are executed in as little as three days, while complex requests are executed within an average of about 10 weeks.

sections.label: Penalties on FIs and VASPs
sections.summary: Maximum financial penalties on FIs and VASPs rose from $800,000 to $5.8 million, with licence revocations and individual accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: For example, the maximum financial penalties imposed on FIs and VASPs increased from $800,000 in the previous ME to $5.8 million this round.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Beyond financial penalties, we have taken other firm measures against FIs and VASPs, including the revocation of licences in egregious cases and holding responsible individuals accountable for lapses.

sections.label: FATF findings on proliferation financing
sections.summary: The FATF found a robust countering proliferation financing legal framework and strong coordination, recommending deeper risk understanding and stronger mitigation for higher-risk sectors.

sentences.text: The FATF has found that Singapore has a robust countering proliferation financing legal framework, and strong coordination and cooperation among Singapore authorities.
The FATF has recommended a deepening of our PF risk understanding and strengthening the risk mitigation measures, particularly for the higher-risk sectors.

sections.label: Scam losses and recovery
sections.summary: In 2025, $913 million was lost to scams and about 15% was recovered, with most funds originating overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As we all know, if we look at 2025, $913 million was lost to scams and only about 15% of it was recovered, given that most of it originated from overseas, and when the funds go overseas, it is quite difficult for us to recover.

sections.label: Singapore MLA issuance and cooperation
sections.summary: Singapore will keep issuing MLAs where appropriate and also pursue international cooperation informally.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Singapore will continue to issue MLAs where it is appropriate, but also pursue international cooperation in informal manner.
